stage: HISTORIE (engine stage 6) - fractal axis + competing frames - cache
disputedNote: Even where this story begins is disputed - picking a start date is itself a position. Frames change emphasis and annotation, never the record.

frames.label: Jun 2026 hike
frames.note: The story begins with the 17 June 2026 announcement that the Bank of Japan policy rate now sits at 1.0%. Read this way, the news is a fresh data point in current monetary policy and a contrast to the Fed and RBA holds the same week. Market wire desks and breaking-news headlines tend to open here.

frames.label: Mar 2024 exit
frames.note: The story begins in March 2024, when the Bank of Japan ended its negative interest rate policy. Read this way, the latest hike is one more scheduled step in a normalization cycle that has been running for over two years. Central-bank trackers and policy analysts often open here.

frames.label: 1995 baseline
frames.note: The story begins in 1995, when Japanese policy rates last sat near this level before the long descent. Read this way, the headline marks the close of a 31-year chapter of ultra-loose money rather than a routine meeting. Long-horizon macro historians and structural commentators tend to open here.

bands.label: Hike to 1.0%
bands.summary: BOJ raises the policy rate to 1.0%, the highest level since 1995, while the Fed and RBA hold steady the same week.

nodes.title: RBA holds cash rate at 4.35%
nodes.what: The Reserve Bank of Australia kept its official cash rate at 4.35% at the June meeting. The board cited a Middle East ceasefire and easing oil-price pressure as factors reducing the urgency to move, while flagging that inflation risks remain. Markets priced the decision as a pause rather than a turn.

nodes.title: Bank of Japan raises policy rate to 1.0%
nodes.what: The Bank of Japan announced a hike that lifts its policy rate to 1.0%, the highest setting since 1995. The bank pointed to sustained wage growth and inflation running at or above its 2% target as conditions for tightening. The decision continues the normalization path that began with the March 2024 exit from negative rates.
nodes.disputed: CGTN frames the move as a routine step in a slow normalization cycle backed by wage and price data; Taipei Times emphasizes the 31-year-high headline and the break from decades of ultra-loose policy.

nodes.title: US Federal Reserve holds rates for the fourth time this year
nodes.what: The Federal Reserve left its target range unchanged at the June FOMC meeting, the fourth consecutive hold of 2026. Officials pointed to mixed inflation and labor data and to uncertainty over tariff pass-through as reasons to wait. The decision arrived hours after the BOJ hike, sharpening the contrast between the two policy paths.
nodes.disputed: The Guardian describes the hold as a cautious wait-and-see stance amid political pressure on the Fed; CGTN presents it as a steady continuation of an extended pause cycle.

bands.label: Exit from negative rates
bands.summary: BOJ ends its negative interest rate policy and runs a slow series of hikes as inflation and wage growth persist.

nodes.title: BOJ ends negative interest rate policy
nodes.what: The Bank of Japan's Policy Board voted to raise the short-term policy rate from minus 0.1% to a range of zero to 0.1%, ending the negative interest rate regime introduced in January 2016. The same decision scrapped yield curve control of 10-year government bond yields and halted purchases of exchange-traded funds and J-REITs. Governor Kazuo Ueda framed the move as a first step away from the extraordinary easing framework built under his predecessor.

cites.l: Bank of Japan monetary policy decisions

nodes.title: Policy rate raised to around 0.25%
nodes.what: At the late-July meeting, the BOJ raised the uncollateralized overnight call rate target to around 0.25%, its second hike of the cycle. The Board also outlined a plan to taper the pace of Japanese government bond purchases over the following years. Ueda signalled that further increases were possible if the economic and price outlook tracked the BOJ's projections.

cites.l: Bank of Japan monetary policy decisions

nodes.disputed: Some market commentators describe the decision as a calibrated normalization step consistent with the BOJ's published outlook; others describe it as a hawkish surprise that policy desks had not priced in, citing the speed of the subsequent yen move.

nodes.title: Global sell-off and yen carry-trade unwind
nodes.what: In the days after the July hike, the Nikkei 225 fell sharply in its largest single-day points drop on record, while the yen strengthened against the dollar and global risk assets sold off. Investors and analysts linked the move to a rapid unwinding of yen-funded carry trades. Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida said days later that the BOJ would not raise rates while markets were unstable, language that traders read as a partial walk-back.
nodes.disputed: Market strategists describe the episode as a carry-trade unwind triggered by the BOJ's hike colliding with weak U.S. data; BOJ officials describe it as a volatility event driven mainly by external factors rather than by the policy decision itself.

nodes.title: Policy rate raised to around 0.5%
nodes.what: The BOJ raised the policy rate to around 0.5%, the highest level since the 2008 global financial crisis. The Board cited continued progress on the 2% inflation target and stronger wage growth confirmed in the annual shunto round. Ueda again said future moves would depend on data, while the quarterly Outlook Report revised up the inflation projection.

cites.l: Bank of Japan monetary policy decisions

nodes.title: Extended pause through most of 2025
nodes.what: After the January 2025 hike, the BOJ held the policy rate at around 0.5% across subsequent meetings through the year, citing uncertainty about external demand, the impact of U.S. tariff policy, and the durability of wage gains. Successive Outlook Reports kept the inflation forecast near or above the 2% target while flagging downside risks to growth. Officials signalled that further normalization was conditional on confirming the wage-price cycle.

nodes.title: Hike to 1.0% closes the band
nodes.what: At the June 2026 meeting, the BOJ raised the policy rate to 1.0%, the highest level since 1995. The same week, the U.S. Federal Reserve and the Reserve Bank of Australia left their own rates unchanged, sharpening the contrast with Japan's continuing normalization. The decision opens the current band of the timeline.

cites.l: Bank of Japan monetary policy decisions

bands.label: Abenomics and QQE
bands.summary: Kuroda-era quantitative and qualitative easing under Abenomics locks in sustained ultra-loose policy and a swollen BOJ balance sheet.

nodes.title: Kuroda launches Quantitative and Qualitative Easing
nodes.what: At his first policy meeting as BOJ governor, Haruhiko Kuroda announced a program to double the monetary base in about two years through large-scale purchases of Japanese government bonds, ETFs and J-REITs. The bank set an explicit 2 percent inflation target to be reached in roughly two years, framing the move as a regime change from incremental easing under his predecessor.

nodes.title: Halloween easing expands QQE
nodes.what: In a split 5-4 vote, the BOJ surprised markets by raising its annual JGB purchase pace to about 80 trillion yen and tripling annual ETF and J-REIT buying. The yen fell sharply against the dollar and the Nikkei surged on the day, with the move coinciding with the Government Pension Investment Fund's shift toward more equities.

nodes.title: BOJ adopts negative interest rate policy
nodes.what: The Bank of Japan introduced a minus 0.1 percent rate on a portion of commercial bank reserves held at the central bank, becoming the first major Asian central bank to take a policy rate below zero. The decision passed 5-4 and was framed as a way to push inflation toward the 2 percent target after QQE alone had failed to deliver it.
nodes.disputed: BOJ officials described the step as a necessary additional tool to combat deflationary pressure; Japanese bank lobby groups and several dissenting board members described it as a measure that would compress bank margins without lifting prices.

nodes.title: Yield Curve Control introduced
nodes.what: The BOJ shifted the framework from a quantity target to one anchored on interest rates, pledging to keep the 10-year JGB yield around zero percent while maintaining the minus 0.1 percent short-term rate. The bank also committed to overshoot its 2 percent inflation target, a step it called QQE with Yield Curve Control.

nodes.title: YCC band widened in surprise move
nodes.what: The BOJ widened the allowed trading band for the 10-year JGB yield from plus or minus 0.25 percent to plus or minus 0.5 percent, a change that markets had not anticipated at that meeting. The yen jumped and JGB yields rose, with Kuroda insisting the step was a technical adjustment to improve bond market functioning rather than a policy tightening.
nodes.disputed: BOJ leadership described the move as a market functioning fix that did not signal a rate cycle turn; many bond investors and overseas analysts described it as a de facto first step away from yield curve control.

nodes.title: Kazuo Ueda becomes BOJ governor
nodes.what: Academic economist Kazuo Ueda succeeded Kuroda as governor, the first scholar rather than career central banker or finance ministry official to lead the bank in the postwar era. In early appearances he signalled continuity with ultra-loose policy while opening a broad review of the easing measures used over the previous 25 years.

nodes.title: YCC made more flexible
nodes.what: Under Ueda the BOJ kept the 10-year yield target at zero but said the 0.5 percent cap would be treated as a reference rather than a rigid line, with the bank conducting fixed-rate operations at 1.0 percent. The yen and JGB yields whipsawed as traders parsed whether the change amounted to a tightening signal or further fine-tuning.

bands.label: Lost decades and ZIRP
bands.summary: After the 1995 cut to historic lows, Japan moves through zero interest rate policy and early quantitative easing across two decades of weak growth and deflation.

nodes.title: BOJ cuts official discount rate to 0.5%
nodes.what: The Bank of Japan lowered its official discount rate to 0.5%, then a historic low, as the economy struggled with the aftermath of the asset price collapse and a strong yen. The move set the baseline that the 2026 hike would later be measured against.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Statistics on policy rates

nodes.title: Zero interest rate policy introduced
nodes.what: The BOJ guided the uncollateralized overnight call rate to effectively zero, formally launching the zero interest rate policy. Governor Masaru Hayami framed it as a response to deflationary pressure and weak demand.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Monetary policy releases archive

nodes.title: BOJ lifts the zero rate
nodes.what: The Bank raised the overnight call rate target to around 0.25%, ending the first ZIRP episode over objections from the government. The decision was followed by renewed economic weakness and is frequently revisited in debates over premature tightening.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Monetary policy decisions

nodes.disputed: The BOJ at the time described the move as appropriate given signs of recovery; later academic and government commentary often describes it as a premature exit that contributed to renewed deflation.

nodes.title: Quantitative easing launched
nodes.what: The BOJ shifted its operating target from the call rate to the outstanding balance of current accounts at the Bank, beginning the first formal quantitative easing program. The framework committed to maintaining ample liquidity until core CPI stabilized at or above zero.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Introduction of quantitative easing

nodes.title: Exit from quantitative easing
nodes.what: The BOJ ended the 2001 QE framework and returned to using the uncollateralized overnight call rate as its operating target, citing improving prices. A first rate hike to 0.25% followed in July 2006.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Change in the guideline for money market operations

nodes.title: Rate cut to 0.1% during global financial crisis
nodes.what: As the global financial crisis spread, the BOJ cut its policy rate target to 0.1% and expanded liquidity operations. The move effectively returned Japan to near-zero rates after the short-lived 2006-2008 tightening cycle.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Monetary policy decisions

nodes.title: Comprehensive Monetary Easing introduced
nodes.what: The BOJ set the policy rate at a range of 0 to 0.1% and announced an asset purchase program covering JGBs, corporate bonds, ETFs and J-REITs. The framework, labeled Comprehensive Monetary Easing, marked a return to balance-sheet policy alongside near-zero rates.

cites.l: Bank of Japan - Comprehensive Monetary Easing

nodes.title: 2% inflation target adopted
nodes.what: The BOJ formally adopted a 2% year-on-year CPI inflation target and issued a joint statement with the government on overcoming deflation. The decision set the policy frame that Governor Haruhiko Kuroda would operationalize through QQE that April.
